doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How the themed albums were chosen
summary: Show-tune and songwriter albums arose from suggestions; the Matt Dennis album was his idea via Ken Curtis.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Dave, we were talking about your recordings for Columbia. You made so many of them, many of them based on various themes. You did West Side Story or Time Out or A Tribute to Cole Porter or Dave Does Disney. How were those projects decided upon? Was that you sitting down with the quartet? Or was it George Avakian? Or was it, in the middle of the night you would get an idea? How did you determine the various themes for these projects?

That’s a good question, because I remember somebody would say something like, you should start playing show tunes of some of the most well-known Broadway shows and just do a whole series of those. So we did Cole Porter and . . .
. . . Richard Rogers. Then my favorite is . . .
Who suggested that? Did that come from George Avakian?

That came from me. My friend in the Army taught me all the Matt Dennis tunes. He was Festus in “Gunsmoke.” Ken Curtis. He could sing with the big bands and often took the place of Frank Sinatra or somebody. He was that good.
